topic: Quadratic Equations with Real and Complex Roots
title: No Real Root? Complex Roots Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Throw a ball straight up. It passes 15 m twice, reaches 20 m once, and never reaches 25 m. Each of those questions is a quadratic equation, so why two answers, then one, then none? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) we see that even never has two answers: they just live off the number line.

You will watch the curve y = x² - 4x + c lift as c counts up, while its two roots slide together, touch, and then step off the number line onto the Argand plane as a complex pair. We derive the quadratic formula in five small steps by completing the square, see what happens when b² - 4ac is negative, compare real and complex roots side by side, and meet conjugate pairs. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with x² + x + 1 = 0, the exam trap with the square root of -16, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Note: solving quadratics in the complex number system is in the JEE Main syllabus but not in the current rationalised NCERT text.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.
